Description:
Glutathione (L-γ-glutamyl-L-cysteinyl-glycine) is the tripeptide that cells rely on as their main defence against oxidative stress. In its reduced form, GSH, it is the most abundant non-protein thiol in mammalian cells. Heartland Bio Labs supplies Glutathione for laboratory research in 600mg, 1200mg and 1500mg vials, independently tested for purity and identity.

What Glutathione is

Glutathione is built from glutamate, cysteine and glycine, with an unusual γ-peptide bond between the glutamate side chain and cysteine that protects it from most peptidases. The free thiol on the cysteine does the chemical work: it donates electrons to neutralise reactive oxygen species and is oxidised in the process to glutathione disulfide (GSSG), which glutathione reductase then recycles back to GSH.

Because of that cycle, the GSH/GSSG ratio is one of the most widely used markers of cellular redox state in research. Glutathione is also the substrate for the glutathione S-transferase enzymes that conjugate and clear xenobiotics, and for glutathione peroxidases that reduce lipid peroxides, so it appears across research on detoxification pathways, mitochondrial function, immune cell biology and protein disulfide regulation.

What GHRP-2 is

GHRP-2 was developed in the 1990s as a successor to GHRP-6, part of the series of small synthetic peptides that showed growth hormone could be released through a pathway separate from GHRH. It is used in research on pituitary somatotroph pharmacology, GHS-R1a signalling and the interaction between the ghrelin and GHRH pathways.

Oxytocin is a nine-amino acid peptide hormone made in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary. It was the first peptide hormone to be sequenced and synthesised. Heartland Bio Labs supplies Oxytocin for laboratory research in 5mg and 10mg vials, independently tested for purity and identity.

What Oxytocin is

Vincent du Vigneaud determined oxytocin’s structure and achieved its chemical synthesis in 1953, work recognised with the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1955. Its sequence is Cys-Tyr-Ile-Gln-Asn-Cys-Pro-Leu-Gly-NH2, with a disulfide bridge between the two cysteines forming a six-residue ring and a three-residue tail. Vasopressin shares the same architecture and differs at only two positions.

Oxytocin acts through a single G protein-coupled receptor, OXTR, found in the brain and peripheral tissues. Research spans its classical roles in smooth muscle contraction and lactation, and its central role in social behaviour, bonding and stress-response circuits in animal models, which has made it one of the most studied neuropeptides in behavioural neuroscience.

Epithalamin, a polypeptide preparation from bovine pineal glands, was the starting point; Epithalon was designed from its amino acid composition as a four-residue peptide that could be made synthetically and characterised exactly.

Most interest in Epithalon comes from in vitro reports of increased telomerase activity and telomere elongation in human somatic cell cultures, and from rodent studies on pineal function, melatonin rhythms and markers of ageing. Much of that literature comes from a single research school, which is worth knowing when weighing it, and it is why Epithalon is a common subject of independent replication work in telomere biology.

L-Carnitine is a small quaternary ammonium compound, made in the body from lysine and methionine, that carries long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria so they can be oxidised for energy. Heartland Bio Labs supplies L-Carnitine for laboratory research in 500mg and 1000mg vials, independently tested for purity and identity.

What L-Carnitine is

Fatty acids longer than about 12 carbons cannot cross the inner mitochondrial membrane on their own. In the carnitine shuttle, carnitine palmitoyltransferase I (CPT1) transfers the fatty acyl group from coenzyme A to carnitine on the outer membrane; a translocase moves the acylcarnitine across; and CPT2 transfers the acyl group back to coenzyme A inside the matrix, where β-oxidation takes place. CPT1 is the rate-controlling step and is inhibited by malonyl-CoA, which ties the shuttle to the cell’s overall energy state.

Because of that position, L-carnitine and its acyl esters are used throughout research on fatty acid oxidation, mitochondrial function and skeletal and cardiac muscle metabolism. Acylcarnitine profiles are also a standard readout in metabolic research.

AICAR (acadesine, 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide riboside) is a cell-permeable adenosine analogue and one of the most widely used research tools for activating AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), the cell’s main energy sensor. Heartland Bio Labs supplies AICAR for laboratory research in 2mg, 5mg, 10mg, 50mg and 100mg vials, independently tested for purity and identity.

What AICAR is

Inside the cell, adenosine kinase phosphorylates AICAR to ZMP, the ribonucleotide form. ZMP mimics AMP and binds the AMPK γ subunit, activating the kinase without changing the cell’s actual energy charge. That lets researchers switch on the AMPK pathway pharmacologically and study what follows: increased glucose uptake, fatty acid oxidation, and reduced lipid and protein synthesis.

AICAR became widely known after a 2008 study in mice reported that it increased running endurance in sedentary animals, which led to it being described as an “exercise mimetic” in the research literature. ZMP is also an intermediate in de novo purine synthesis, and AMPK-independent effects through that route are a known consideration when interpreting results.

5-Amino-1MQ (5-amino-1-methylquinolinium) is a small-molecule inhibitor of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), an enzyme highly expressed in fat tissue and liver. What 5-Amino-1MQ is

NNMT transfers a methyl group from S-adenosylmethionine to nicotinamide, producing 1-methylnicotinamide. That reaction consumes nicotinamide that would otherwise be recycled into NAD+, and consumes methyl groups from the cell’s SAM pool. Elevated NNMT expression in adipose tissue has been associated with obesity in animal models, which made it a target of interest in metabolic research.

5-Amino-1MQ is a membrane-permeable quinolinium compound developed as a selective NNMT inhibitor. In published cell and mouse studies, inhibiting NNMT raised intracellular NAD+ and SAM levels in adipocytes and reduced lipogenesis, with diet-induced obese mice showing reduced adipose mass. It is used in research on adipocyte metabolism, NAD+ salvage and cellular methylation balance.

What LIPO-C is

Lipotropic compounds are nutrients that support the export of fat from the liver. The three core components of LIPO-C each play a defined role there. Methionine is the precursor of S-adenosylmethionine, the cell’s main methyl donor. Choline is needed to make phosphatidylcholine, which the liver requires to package triglycerides into VLDL particles for export. Inositol is a component of the phosphatidylinositol lipids involved in membrane signalling and lipid trafficking.

In animal models, deficiency of choline and methionine is a classic way of inducing fatty liver, which is why these compounds are central to research on hepatic lipid metabolism and methyl-donor pathways. B-complex vitamins act as co-factors in the same one-carbon and energy pathways.

IGF-1 LR3 (Long R3 Insulin-like Growth Factor-1) is an 83-amino acid analogue of human IGF-1, engineered to bind poorly to IGF binding proteins so that it stays active far longer in cell culture. What IGF-1 LR3 is

Native IGF-1 is a 70-amino acid growth factor that circulates almost entirely bound to IGF binding proteins (IGFBPs), which limit how much is free to act on the IGF-1 receptor. IGF-1 LR3 makes two changes: the glutamic acid at position 3 is replaced with arginine (the “R3”), and a 13-amino acid extension is added to the N-terminus (the “Long”). Together they sharply reduce binding to IGFBPs, which greatly extends the analogue’s activity in vitro.

That property made IGF-1 LR3 a standard supplement in serum-free cell culture media, including in biopharmaceutical cell lines, and a common tool in research on IGF-1 receptor signalling through the PI3K-Akt and MAPK pathways, cell proliferation, and skeletal muscle cell differentiation.

Heartland Bio Labs supplies PEG MGF for laboratory research in 2mg and 10mg vials, independently tested for purity and identity.

What PEG MGF is

The IGF-1 gene is spliced into several variants. One of them, IGF-1Ec in humans (IGF-1Eb in rodents), is expressed in skeletal muscle in response to mechanical loading and damage, which is why it was named mechano growth factor. Research by Geoffrey Goldspink and colleagues in the 1990s and 2000s suggested that the peptide derived from its unique C-terminal E-domain has activity distinct from mature IGF-1, particularly in activating muscle satellite cells.

The native E-domain peptide breaks down within minutes in biological fluids. Attaching polyethylene glycol (PEGylation) shields it from proteases and slows clearance, which makes PEG MGF usable in research on satellite cell activation, the response of muscle to mechanical load and the distinct roles of IGF-1 splice variants.

Storage and handling

Store lyophilized PEG MGF sealed, dry and protected from light, frozen at −20 °C for long-term storage. Reconstitute with bacteriostatic water or sterile water and keep the solution refrigerated at 2–8 °C, avoiding repeated freeze-thaw cycles.
